subject: Hosted evaluation: bandwidth, rate caps & ops coordination
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation: bandwidth, rate caps & ops coordination

Rajesh — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a short set of asks so we can stand up a hosted evaluation that matches your traffic profile and security needs.

Summary from our call
- Finlytics primary use case: real-time answer generation for customer support agents (short context, multi-turn threads).
- Expected steady-state: ~200 QPS during business hours; peak bursts up to ~1.5k QPS for short windows (10–20 min).
- Average token length: requests ~120 tokens, expected responses ~220 tokens.
- Compliance: SOC2 required; will need audit logs and retention controls.
- Networking: prefer private egress/ingress options for production but OK to start with hosted sandbox for evaluation.

Open items we need from you to size the hosted pilot
1) Confirm expected daily request volume (or monthly token estimate) so we can provision token quotas.
2) Verify whether any customer data will be uploaded as attachments to the prompts (affects caching/retention).
3) Any strict IP allowlist or CIDR ranges for sandbox endpoints?

What I recommend for the pilot (short answer)
- Start with hosted sandbox endpoints (fastest path). We’ll allocate a dedicated evaluation endpoint with a higher baseline rate and prefix KV caching enabled for short-context workloads.
- If Finlytics needs predictable higher sustained throughput and isolation, transition to a Dedicated reservation (monthly commit) after the pilot.
- Private VPC/on‑prem is available if your security team requires customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS.

Attachments: I attached a one‑page hosted_quickstart_matrix.xlsx (endpoint mapping, default rate caps, token quotas) and traffic_profile.csv (sample format). Also attaching sandbox-access-guide.pdf we use for credentials.

Next steps (proposed)
- You: confirm the three items above (volume, attachments in prompts, allowlist).
- We: provision a sandbox endpoint, share credentials, and give a short ops runbook for rate limits and KV caching.
- Ops call: schedule 30m with our infra lead (Neha) to walk the sandbox and talk rate/backpressure behavior.

Thanks — I’ll draft a short mutual action plan when we confirm the volume.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: bandwidth, rate caps & ops coordination

Ben — thanks, useful summary. A few clarifications from our side so Neha can size things correctly:  

1) Volume: target is ~14M tokens/day initially (we expect growth). Peak QPS estimate comes from scheduled marketing blasts that spike activity; steady-state will be ~150–220 QPS.
2) Attachments: occasionally yes — we do pass short CSV snippets as context for enrichment (~5% of requests). Data won't be PII in pilot, but it’s still proprietary.
3) Allowlist: we can provide a set of static IP ranges. For the sandbox we prefer restricting to our office CIDR and the VPN exit IPs; I can send the list by EOD.

Also can you confirm the following about hosted sandbox endpoints:
- Per-endpoint default RPS and burst behavior (what to expect before we request increases).
- Token-per-minute ceilings for a single API key (to plan client-side throttling).
- How prefix/KV caching will be configured and whether it persists across restarts.

If hosted sandbox can meet predictable bursts with KV caching and transparent logs, we can proceed quickly. If not, we need to discuss Dedicated reserved capacity.

I can join a 30m ops call — suggest Wed 13 Sep 09:00 PT.

Thanks,
Rajesh Patel
Head of Product
Finlytics
rajesh.patel@finlytics.com

Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation: bandwidth, rate caps & ops coordination

Rajesh — good context, thanks. Short answers to your bullets and a concrete pilot plan below.

Rate & burst behavior (hosted sandbox defaults)
- Sandbox endpoint (evaluation) default: 100 RPS per endpoint, with short-term burst capability to ~1k RPS for authenticated sandbox clients (subject to fair-use windows).
- Production endpoints (standard hosted) default: 500 RPS per model endpoint; can be raised with quota request or by moving to Dedicated.
- Token-per-minute default per API key: 3M tokens/minute for sandbox; production is higher and can be tuned. We will surface real-time token usage metrics in the console.

KV/prefix caching details
- We enable prefix caching for repeated short-context requests. Cache is sticky to the endpoint instance pool and persists across short restarts (minutes). For long-term persistence (across redeploys) we can enable durable KV (requires Dedicated/Private option).

Security & logs
- Hosted provides structured audit logs (request metadata, model used, token counts). For SOC2 evidence we can export logs to your S3 and pin retention policy for the pilot.
- If you require customer-managed keys or private networking, Private VPC is the right path.

Pilot proposal (steps)
1) We provision a dedicated evaluation endpoint in hosted sandbox with higher baseline (200 RPS) and KV caching turned on.
2) We share sandbox credentials and an allowlist IP config you provide.
3) Neha will run a 30m ops session to show backpressure behavior and how to read token/latency dashboards.
4) After 1 week of traffic, we’ll review metrics and recommend either (a) increase hosted quotas, (b) reserve Dedicated capacity, or (c) migrate to Private VPC.

Docs & attachments
- I’ve attached the sandbox-access-guide.pdf with steps for credential rotation and example requests. Also included the hosted_quickstart_matrix.xlsx mapping the endpoints to default quotas and a sample traffic_profile.csv for your usage.

Proposed times
- Ops call: Wed 13 Sep, 09:00 PT (Neha and I). Please confirm or propose another time.

If that plan works, I’ll open a mutual action plan in HubSpot and create a short ticket for quota/provisioning.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
